answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to solve a proof-of-work puzzle whose result is bound to a public key and a time window; peers reject duplicate or invalid proofs. The trellis of linked challenges lets nodes check admission cheaply, while a canyon of accumulated work separates costly identities from free aliases. An attacker can still create keys, but must spend real compute and electricity for each one, and repeat that expense as the cedar of the network’s difficulty adjusts.
